**Premise 1:** (S ∨ P) ↔ (S ↔ P)

- S=T, P=T: (T) ↔ (T) = T ✓
- S=T, P=F: (T) ↔ (F) = F
- S=F, P=T: (T) ↔ (F) = F
- S=F, P=F: (F) ↔ (T) = F

Premise 1 is **only true when S = T and P = T**. So premise 1 forces both S and P to be true, i.e., S ∧ P.

**Premise 2:** R ↔ Q — This states R and Q have the same truth value (already given).

**Combining both premises**, the conclusion is:

<answer>S ∧ P ∧ (R ↔ Q)</answer>
